The titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names. This has always been clear throughout this messy, injury-ravaged men’s season but it was underlined in the grand finale as Carlos Alcaraz ended his campaign with a statement victory, defeating the top-ranked player, Alexander Zverev, 6-2, 7-6 (7) to win the ATP Finals for the first time.

So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year.

items.title: Kildunne returns to haunt Harlequins as Bristol get PWR season off to a flyer
items.summary:
• Harlequins 21-48 Bristol

  • Full-back marks debut with two tries against former club

As women’s rugby grows, more scrutiny will follow and Ellie Kildunne has felt that over the past few months. Her performances have been put under a microscope and she was dropped to the bench in England’s final two WXV matches in October, but she silenced her critics with a stellar and trademark performance in her Bristol debut. The full-back did it under significant pressure too, as she returned to the Stoop five months after her shock exit from Harlequins and helped Bristol beat her former side in their Premiership Women’s Rugby opener.

The Bristol head coach, Scott Lawson, had thrown his full backing behind Kildunne in the buildup, saying that being at the West Country club would “bring the best” out of the 27-year-old, and if her debut is anything to go by he will be proved right. The World Cup winner not only scored two tries but was also a linchpin in Bristol’s attack. Her gamechanging reputation was felt among her former teammates as she drew multiple defenders to her whenever she had the ball, meaning the wings on her outside had a lot more joy. The back three looked formidable with both wings, Reneeqa Bonner and Millie David, also scoring two tries apiece.

items.title: Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red
items.summary:
Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at ­Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for ­denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again.

Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liver­pool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s history.

items.summary:
• Former player known for partnership with Chris Berman

  • Jackson was member of Broncos for 14 seasons

ESPN is mourning “one of the most influential and beloved figures” in the broadcaster’s history after the death of Tom Jackson at the age of 75.

Jackson played for the Denver Broncos for 14 seasons at linebacker, and was a two-time All-Pro selection, before turning to broadcasting after his playing career ended in 1986. He was a key part of ESPN’s NFL coverage, most notably alongside Chris Berman, for 29 years before his retirement in 2016.

items.title: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts
items.summary:
The head coach said he has watched videos from Eddie Jones’ time in charge to help England begin matches strongly

Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation: “We are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off.” And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep.

Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand.

items.t: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts

items.title: Marc Márquez claims record-equalling eighth MotoGP world title in Portugal
items.summary:
• Spaniard matches Giacomo Agostini’s premier-class tally

  • Márquez defends his title despite double surgery in May

Marc Márquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP world title at the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday, after his eighth-placed finish proved enough to establish an unassailable lead in the overall standings.

The Ducati rider needed to finish in the top nine in Sunday’s race and despite starting second on the grid, Márquez rode with caution to finish eighth and seal the title with a round to spare. The Spaniard’s eighth premier-class title puts him alongside the great Giacomo Agostini at the top of motorcycle racing’s all-time standings.

items.title: The footballer-turned-BookTuber who made an obscure Tolstoy novella a belated bestseller
items.summary:
Once named the best player in Brazil, Gustavo Scarpa’s literature obsession has inspired thousands to become bookworms

Julián Scatolaro noticed something odd was occurring when several people came into his bookshop over the space of a few days, all asking for Leo Tolstoy’s novella The Death of Ivan Ilyich.

The 35-year-old, who owns a bookshop in the small Argentine city of Chajarí, 311 miles from Buenos Aires, said the sudden interest in a book written in 1886 was surprising enough. But this was particularly strange because when his customers ask for works by the Russian writer, they usually want War and Peace. In a video he posted about the mystery, he called it the “Tolstoy enigma”.

items.title: Tyson Fury looks back: ‘Once the Anthony Joshua fight is over, what will I do next? Walking the dog ain’t gonna cut it’
items.summary:
The former heavyweight boxing champion on falling in love at first sight, being diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and the much-anticipated match

Born in Manchester in 1988, Tyson Fury – known as the Gypsy King – is a former unified heavyweight world champion. He turned professional in 2008 and in 2015 defeated the long-reigning champion, Wladimir Klitschko, to claim the WBA, IBF, WBO and Ring magazine heavyweight titles. He made a comeback in 2020, and his long-awaited final fight is on 11 December against Anthony Joshua. He appears with his wife, Paris, and seven children in the docuseries At Home With the Furys. A documentary charting his life, Fury, is out on Netflix on 27 November.

This was a race unique to this season and not seen in the sport for a long time, an old-school duel of slipstreaming and the sort of over-the-top extravaganza perfect for Las Vegas, Cirque du Soleil fashioned from carbon fibre and noise.

Record-breaking win suggests Steve Borthwick’s side are realising their enormous potential at last

Something’s coming. Oh yes. They will be able to hear its approaching footsteps in Edinburgh and Dublin and Paris and Cardiff, the tremors will ripple through Johannesburg and Sydney all the way to Auckland, where they will finally arrive sometime when the New Zealand public wakes up to find out all about what happened to their team here at Twickenham. After years of being oh so ordinary, England are on their way at long last to looking like the sort of team their depth of talent and wealth of resources has always suggested they ought to be.

When they beat Australia, everyone said how woeful the Wallabies were, when they thrashed Japan, all the talk was about how far the Brave Blossoms had fallen, but there are no caveats when you beat New Zealand like this. There’s no such thing as an easy win against the All Blacks. And no such thing, either, as a bad All Blacks team, even if this one’s a long way short of their best. It was a record victory, the 25-point margin eight more than England managed to win by in their famous victory here in 2012. Honestly, it could, maybe should, have been by more. England had…

items.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
items.summary:
The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.
